data.body:
ROUND 10'S OPEN ITEMS, RESOLVED AGAINST LANDED CODE — recording before the split so S1/S2 start from
facts rather than from plan text.

FINDING 1 (the design hole: WHAT ESCAPES WHEN THE 429 RETRY CAP IS EXHAUSTED). **Answer:
`BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429` — never the raw `JIRAError`.** This is not a preference, it is
what the existing boundary already does and what J10 pinned. `_with_connection_retry` catches
`_jira_http_error_types()` and does `raise _as_backend_http_error(exc) from exc`
(transport.py:243-246 region), and `_as_backend_http_error` reads `.status_code` into
`BackendHTTPError.code` using urllib's spelling SO THAT the core's existing
`except urllib.error.HTTPError` branches classify a DC failure exactly as they classify a Cloud one
— e.g. a 404 read reaching `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` is seen as `_DELETED`.
So the requirement on S2 is precise and testable: the exhausted-cap path must funnel through the SAME
translation, yielding `BackendHTTPError(code=429)`. A test should assert the TYPE and the CODE, and
should also assert that `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` does NOT escape — the vendor type leaking past
the adapter boundary is the actual regression risk, and a test that only checks "it raised" would
pass while that happened. Note the degradation rule too: a library error with no usable status
becomes `code=0`, which no core branch mistakes for a 404 or a success.

FINDING 3 (asserted from 9263's PLAN TEXT, not landed code — "re-verify once 1129 lands"). **1129 HAS
LANDED; re-verified on `origin/main`: `_paged_search` DOES route through `_call_logged`.** It is
defined at transport.py:421 and its body calls `_call_logged(...)` wrapping
`self._client.search_issues(...)`. Its callers on main are the project reads (`:455`, `:469`) and the
parent-map read (`:567`). So the opt-in question in finding 2 is a real fork with a real target, not
a hypothetical.

TRANSPORT SIZE, measured rather than remembered: `transport.py` is **789 lines on `origin/main`**
right now, against the LOCKED 800 cap — ELEVEN lines of headroom. That is the fact that forces S1:
the 429 policy cannot be added in place. (Recording the number and its source because this file's LOC
has been misquoted twice in this epic — the earlier "792 vs 789" disagreement was a pre-/post-9263
base difference, and now that 9263 is merged the two readings have converged at 789.)

CARRY-OVER FOR S2's PLAN, unchanged from round 10 and still unaddressed: finding 2 (does
`_paged_search` always opt in, or accept and forward a flag — opposite failure modes) and finding 5
(enumerate the ~10 non-opting mutation sites instead of an ellipsis). Finding 4 was my own
arithmetic error: Scope says ELEVEN read call sites, the table has TEN rows.
